title: Double bass
summary: Four open strings (E1, A1, D2, G2) and three stopped notes. D3 is bowed at 0.1286 of its sounding length and locks to one fast slip per period at all three bow cells (read with the flyback reader, which does not count slow secondary slips; the raw count at the third cell is two per period); it sounds 8.0 cents sharp of equal temperament on the 23-layer rib (7.1 on the 6-layer one). Eb2, stopped on the A string with 512 body modes and the bass's own bow-hair row, sounds 7.1 cents sharp of equal temperament and locks to one slip per period at the bow's centre in 69 of 74 periods. Db4, stopped on the D string with 512 body modes, the bass's own bow-hair row and the bow at one eleventh of the sounding length, sounds its note 14.4 cents sharp of equal temperament on the 23-layer rib, and its bow no longer locks: the centre cell slips not at all in 64 of 265 periods, once in 114 and twice in 87, where the page with the violin row slipped once in 263 of 264. A1, D2 and G2 at 512 modes carry the bass's own row too. A1 slips fast twice per period at all three bow cells on the 23-layer rib (the flyback reader; the page before it, on the 6-layer rib, slipped once per period, as the 256-mode page did), and the centre cell of D2 slips four to six times and of G2 two to four times per period (raw counts on the 23-layer rib, which include slow secondary slips and have not been re-read with the flyback reader). The body is a computed shell that keeps its lowest 512 modes on every page: to about 2.88 kHz on the 6-layer rib of Eb2, and on the 23-layer rib of A1, D3, E1, D2, G2 and Db4 to a frequency not computed yet (the 23-layer modes are computed to 1.45 kHz so far). Above the last mode it neither moves nor radiates, so the pages are much darker than the recordings from about 3 kHz up. The rib is not converged at 6 layers: going to 23 layers moves the median of the first 100 coupled modes down 76 cents (4.3 %) and of ranks 201 to 257 down 164 cents (9.0 %), and the 23-layer rib is within about 0.24 % of its limit on the first 100 modes and about 1 % at 1.2 to 1.45 kHz by extrapolation; above 1.45 kHz it is not shown. It is spruce and maple shell with a 116 L air cavity through the f-holes, from Johannsson's printed bass dimensions on the cello shell route, not a scan; wood below 150 Hz is a declared extrapolation. The bow is a 10 mm ribbon (16 mm, the bass's own row, on A1, E1, Eb2, Db4, D2 and G2; D3 keeps the violin row) with hair compliance on the measured rosin curve (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13). The after-length is a sixth of the speaking length or a sixth x 116/115, a ratio borrowed from the cello.
physics_present: computed double-bass shell body: spruce top and bass bar, maple back, ribs and bridge, from Johannsson's printed bass dimensions on the cello shell route; every page keeps the lowest 512 modes, ending at about 2.88 kHz on the 6-layer rib (Eb2) and at a frequency not yet computed on the 23-layer rib (A1, D3, E1, D2, G2, Db4); the rib is meshed with 6 layers through its height on the first group and 23 on the second; first structural mode 106 Hz
air cavity of 116 L breathing through the f-holes (a physical neck); coupled air mode 61 Hz
wood from the measured spruce (from 100 Hz) and maple (from 150 Hz) packs, with the lower band edge moved to 90 Hz as a declared extrapolation, not a measurement
Thomastik Spirocore Orchestra 4/4 medium strings (maker's tension table, line mass and gauges) at a 1.100 m speaking length, bending modes in two polarisations, with a bending stiffness

bow of finite width: a 10 mm ribbon of 3 cells with hair compliance (Pitteroff and Woodhouse 1998); on A1, E1, Eb2, Db4, D2 and G2 the bass's own row, a 16 mm ribbon with 127 hairs in contact over 0.53 m, which gives the S 1.9e5 N/m and D 31 kg/s they print for a bass bow; D3 carries the violin row (S 6.1e4 N/m, D 10 kg/s)
friction law measured on real rosin (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13), a steady sliding curve
static compliance of the omitted body modes at the bridge and under the bow (exact static Green)
after-length (bridge to tailpiece): one sixth of the speaking length (E1) or one sixth x 116/115 (A1, D2, G2), the printed bowed-string rule with the cello's 116 mm ratio borrowed
a bow gesture on a fixed schedule: a 0.15 s ramp to the note's force at 0.15 m/s, then a 20 ms lift; each page states its bow force

a finger stop on the stopped notes (D3, Eb2): a normal contact on the string at the equal-tempered station; its limit (1000 N on D3 and Eb2) is the solver's guard, not a finger's force, and no print gives a finger force
physics_missing: body modes above the 512th: above the last one (about 2.88 kHz on the 6-layer rib) the body neither moves nor radiates, and the pages are much darker than the recordings from about 3 kHz up. D2 reads 10 of 14 at 512 modes with the bass row against 12 at 256, mostly because the grader reads a shorter sustain on that clip

the rib's convergence: rank by rank in frequency, going from 6 layers to 12 moves the median of the first 100 coupled modes down 58 cents (3.3 %), ranks 101 to 200 by 104 cents (5.8 %) and ranks 201 to 257 by 123 cents (6.9 %); going from 12 layers to 23 moves them a further 13 cents (0.73 %), 28 cents (1.6 %) and 37 cents (2.1 %); a power law in the layer count puts the 23-layer modes about 0.24 % above their limit on the first 100 and about 1.1 % over ranks 201 to 257 (1.2 to 1.45 kHz), an extrapolation; above 1.45 kHz the 23-layer modes are not computed, and the step from 6 layers to 12 moves the 256 modes above the first window by 164 cents (9.0 %) and 203 cents (11.1 %), so the upper part of the 512 modes is not shown to be converged. Against the 6-layer pages graded on the same footing (the live page's raw render), the 23-layer rib reads D3 8 of 14 as before (strict 8 against 8), E1 on the bass hair at 11 N 3 against 6 (strict 2 against 5), D2 8 against 10 (strict 8 against 9), G2 11 against 12 (strict 11 against 12), Db4 7 against 6 (strict 6 against 6) and A1 13 against 13 (strict 13 against 13); the A1 page on the 23-layer rib slips fast twice per period at all three cells where the page it replaces slips once, and its gaps grow on the centroid (1.1 to 6.1 semitones), odd/even balance (1.4 to 5.8 dB), harmonics-to-noise (1.1 to 3.2 dB), spectral distance (13.8 to 14.9), STFT distance (14.7 to 15.6), harmonic level pattern (11.9 to 12.6), third-octave envelope (7.0 to 7.8) and fundamental frequency (1.3 to 1.8 cents); this A1 render is also on a later build of the solver (nine more commits to the contact directory than the 6-layer page's binary), and no render separates that from the rib

stopped notes: D3 sits 14 cents sharp of its recording, and its bow locks only at the centre, the third port slipping twice in most periods; Eb2 sits within 0.5 cents of its recording, but its fourth harmonic is 23 dB under the recording's and its second and third 7 dB over; with four changes at once (512 modes, the bass hair row, the 1000 N guard and a raised-limit binary) this render cannot say which let it finish; Db4 sits 25.3 cents sharp of its recording (which is 10.9 cents flat of equal temperament), its harmonics are 13 to 57 dB under the recording's from H3 to H12 (H3 by 18 dB, H4 13, H6 13, H7 14, H9 48, H10 33, H11 57, H12 38), so the centroid is 383 Hz against 789 Hz, and with the bass row its bow does not lock and its attack reads 67 ms against the recording's 5 ms

the bass bow-hair row (Pitteroff and Woodhouse 1998, S 1.9e5 N/m, D 31 kg/s) did not raise the grade on A1, Db4, D2 or G2, against the same card with the violin row graded the same way: A1 13 of 14 against 13 (strict 13 against 13), its bow slipping fast once per period at all three cells on the 6-layer rib, as the 256-mode page did (flyback reader); Db4 6 of 14 against 6 (strict 6 against 5) with its lock gone, its attack at 94 ms against 11 ms and its fundamental 24.9 cents from the recording's against 21.8; D2 10 against 10 (strict 9 against 10: the third-octave envelope moves in, the wavelet spectrum out); G2 12 against 12 (strict 12 against 12). Eb2 reads 12 against 10, with four changes at once as stated above. D2, G2 and Db4 do not lock with the bass row at the forces they had with the violin hair (raw counts, not re-read with the flyback reader); Eb2 locks in 69 of 74 periods and E1 at 11 N in 39 of 39

pages with the bass row that did not post: D3 at 512 modes graded 6 of 14 against 8 and lost the lock it had (three to five slips in a period, in 140 periods), and on the 23-layer rib at 3.86 N it grades 7 of 14 (strict 6) against 8 (8), losing harmonics-to-noise (19.7 dB against the recording's 29.2) and, strictly, the odd/even balance, with one fast slip per period at all three cells (flyback reader), so D3 stays on the violin row; E1 with the bass row at the violin-hair force of 7.28 N graded 5 of 14 against 6 and lost its lock (one slip in only 7 of 39 periods), so E1 plays 11 N, the lowest of 11, 14 and 17 N at which a short render of the bass-hair card held the lock (39 of 39 periods; 14 N and 17 N did not), and its 23-layer render grades 3 of 14 (strict 2) against 6 (5), with 39 of 39 periods locked; the bass-hair forces of D2, G2 and Db4 are the violin-hair ones and were not re-laddered

the melody's C3 at 512 modes with the bass row (0.6 s) was refused by the engine 0.358 s in, all three ribbon cells sticking: modal contact residual 2.61e-10 N exceeds 2.16e-10 N after 821 iterations; the melody stays on the violin row

a measured bass: the body is mapped from a maker's published specification onto the il Cannone specimen tables, not scanned; the bass bar is moved 18.1 mm inward to clear the f-hole (no source prints that position); the bridge is a uniform 152.6 g shell; the 1.070 m of a 3/4 instrument is not modelled
measured wood properties below 150 Hz (maple) and 100 Hz (spruce)
string loss: none is printed for these strings, so the cards carry none and the notes ring on after the bow lifts
string torsion: the cards carry no twist modes
the rosin's temperature and contact history: the friction is a steady sliding curve with no thermal or third-body memory
a printed double-bass after-length: the 116/115 ratio is borrowed from the cello
player variation: bow speed and force follow a fixed schedule
blocked: the melody's C3 on the bass row (refused 0.358 s in by the modal contact residual).
